intelligence.human_view: Every room in a house has the same walls and the same roof — only the middle changes: the kitchen has a stove, the bedroom has a bed, the mail room has the letters. That is the One-System Law: one frame, the Hub, and a function is a change of the center, nothing else. The Messenger rounds kept building new houses instead of furnishing the room — a cover here, pills there, a different family — and each drift had to be repaired by another round. The law ends the drift at the root: start from the Hub frame, and you cannot build a different family by accident. And the same eye test judges the work: if the page looks exactly the same in the first second, nothing changed — however many checks it passed.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine one big kingdom. It has one strong spine in the middle. All the parts work at the same time. The frame around it is gold and purple. It has a jewel in each corner. You take the real bricks to build it. You never make a clay copy. One click builds a whole new page. That is how the kingdom grows.
intelligence.grandma_view: A family is like that too: one family, shared table, shared stories — and still, you don't open your sister's letters. Togetherness was never the same as no boundaries. It's good to see a computer system finally written that way round.
intelligence.naya_view: ONE SYSTEM: THE FRAME STAYS THE HUB AND ONLY THE CENTER MORPHS INTO THE FUNCTION YOU'RE IN. A ROUND THAT CHANGES NOTHING THE EYE SEES IN THE FIRST SECOND HAS CHANGED NOTHING. ALIGN, DO NOT REBUILD.
